from: docs/design/balance-program/60-game-review.md section 8 (calls G-1 to G-88, being renamed GR-1 to GR-88; 61-review-audit.md)
the phase B patches in tools/balance-program/patches/
rule: ONE FILE. A proposal the matrix can model names its patch (a scratch-copy derivation, never an edit of the tree) or its derived reading; `recommended` is on in the proposed game the dashboard opens on; `shipsWith` pairs are flagged when one is on without the other; `after` is the ruled order. `excludes`: an alternative to those proposals (it rewrites what they rewrite), so turning it on turns them off. A proposal the matrix cannot model says why.

frame.title: All four heroes from the start, one Premium per account
frame.ruled: Tyler 2026-11-21 ~09:50 UTC, executive decision (rulings of record); settles GR-2; not built yet, waits for the build plan
frame.label: RULED
frame.effect: identity on every hunt cell: the matrix never charged for a hero slot. Its party cells are your own two, three and four from the party Level (STD.PARTIES fromLevel 5, the Sewer's Level), and its gold readings are hunt gold less store buys. The proposed game therefore already plays your own four from day 1 with no slot purchase in any gold or pace cell.
frame.note: Retired on the proposed side: the day each hero slot arrives (X1) and the slot-price guard cells G9 and G20, which read the 400k / 1.5M / 4M prices this ruling replaces. Premium is not a matrix input (the stamina day is stamina-day.mjs), so one Premium per account moves no cell. The slot sink was about 5.5M of the 5.9M standing sinks; sinks as band gold (R16) stay not modelled until they are re-planned.

frame.title: Party buffs are part of the game; no party-size targets
frame.ruled: Tyler 2026-11-21, verbatim: "Let's just not really worry about the targets for solo / group stuff. The same party buffs will apply, it's a no brainer to hunt together."
frame.label: RULED
frame.effect: identity on every cell: the party buffs the proposed game plays are the ones in the tree, as they stand
frame.note: Gone from the dashboard: every solo-against-group, pair, trio and four-multiple target (a head against a lone hero, a party's multiple of the lone contract, the party path against the lone path, and S11, the four after deaths against the lone hero). The matrix still plays parties and the tool still reads them; nothing is judged on party size. Death on the harder tiers is read against the same party on Normal (P9) in the deaths panel.

frame.title: Deadly is for watching or gambling: its death band and its lost hours stand
frame.label: RULED
frame.effect: every cell plays the real death rule and records deaths, the hunts that ended early and the hunting time lost; the four on the harder tiers is played both ways (the rest hunting on, the default; and all coming home: the matrix's leave block)
frame.note: The Deadly death band (S6, 50 to 100 a 1,000 hours for a mid four) stands and the lost time is accepted.

proposals.title: A gear curve as a game formula
proposals.label: HYPOTHESIS
proposals.layer: formula (plan: the kit a cell wears)
proposals.note: Weapon and armor from Level 110 on the line (Dawnsteel x the band Level / 110), a band every +24% (110, 136, 169, 210, 260, 322, 400, then on). LOW one band back. The band size is HYPOTHESIS until one band is played. Uniques spending a budget (R11) are not modelled: past 110 every MID and BiS piece is the line piece

proposals.title: What a kill pays
proposals.label: COMPUTED
proposals.note: XP a health point = the pace contract over the reference kill-health an hour (a lone MID hammer on Normal, measured on the matrix and fitted c x L^d), so the 15 per-ground XP fits, the floor fit and the 0.4 exponent go. Party grounds keep their type with XP a kill at two thirds of a plain kill (was 0.8)

proposals.title: One tier table for every ground

proposals.note: One tier table: the per-ground tier dials go (pull capacity stays, it is geography) and so does the floor-16 pull rule

proposals.title: The Level table
proposals.label: COMPUTED
proposals.note: Your table of hours is the law: the XP a Level costs is the ruled hours (log-linear between the ruled points, on at the last slope past 1,000) times the pace contract times the pace seat's measured multiple. Levels 1 to 10 keep today's steps (27-2). Not the withdrawn power law (progression-1)

proposals.title: Death past Level 100
proposals.label: COMPUTED
proposals.note: RULED (S-5, B): 6% flat, three Blessings, then a new one past the third whenever a blessed death would cost over about five hunted hours (the Levels measured for it: 100, 185, 275, 400; each halves what a blessed death still takes). Played in every cell since the measuring tool's step 1 (progression-grid.mjs buildCell blessedShare; Blessings 4 to 7 are bought at no price: their gold is not designed). The five hours is a guess until a real death rate exists

proposals.title: Talents: a point every five Levels, four stat lines played
proposals.label: HYPOTHESIS
proposals.note: BASELINE, not a bonus (chapter 10, 5.1): every harness hero carries the suggested build of its way (talents.mjs SUGGESTED, the plan rule of 3.4) and the Level law and the kill reward are derived with it in. Played through four seams planted on the scratch copy: Force on the permanent damage key, Footing on the Defense rating, Grit on max health, Reserve on max mana. Linger and every unlock are NOT MODELLED (see notModelled); a way whose plan spends on Linger (the axes) plays those points as nothing. PROVISIONAL sizes: ceilings 10 / 12 / 12 / 15%, half at rank 10. The contrast builds A to D are the matrix's talents block. The to-hit floor owed by CORE-4 bounds Footing and is not written: the matrix prints where it would bite
